title: Model Capability Manifest and Runtime Discovery Standard
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the Model Capability Manifest (MCM) and the runtime discovery protocol Redwood components must use to advertise, query, and validate model capabilities. The MCM standard enables deterministic routing, cost-aware selection, graceful fallback, and coherent observability across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to all model artifacts served through Redwood runtime (hosted API, dedicated pools, private runtime sidecar).
- Targets: model onboarding service, runtime router, orchestration, SDKs, and the Console.
- Exclusions: transient experimental artifacts not used in production.

Motivation:
Current routing and fallback are largely ad-hoc: handwritten tags, opaque release notes, and ad-hoc tests. The MCM provides a machine-readable single source-of-truth for:
- feature support (streaming, function-calling, tool-hinting)
- performance envelopes (p50/p95 token latency and throughput by sequence-length buckets)
- cost and resource profile (tokens-per-second estimate, GPU memory footprint)
- behavioral flags (deterministic seed, sampling-stability, safety-filtered)

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Standardize capability descriptors to allow automated routing and fallbacks.
  - Make runtime discovery low-latency and cacheable with clear invalidation.
  - Surface capability mismatches to observability and pre-deployment checks.
- Non-goals:
  - Replace user-facing natural-language release notes.
  - Enforce model behavior beyond declared guarantees (we validate presence, not absolute correctness).

Specification

1) Model Capability Manifest (MCM) schema (v1.0)
The MCM is a JSON-LD-like manifest attached to each model version. Example: 

{
  "mcm_version": "1.0",
  "model_id": "redwood/pythia-6k:2026-01-15",
  "capabilities": {
    "generation": { "streaming": true, "max_tokens": 8192 },
    "chat": { "roles": ["user", "assistant", "system"] },
    "functions": { "supports_function_calling": true, "max_function_defs": 10 },
    "structured_output": { "schema_validation": "json-schema-07" }
  },
  "performance_profiles": [
    {
      "profile_name": "default",
      "seq_len_bucket": "0-256",
      "p50_ms": 12,
      "p95_ms": 45,
      "throughput_rps": 180
    },
    {
      "profile_name": "long-context",
      "seq_len_bucket": "2048-4096",
      "p50_ms": 90,
      "p95_ms": 300,
      "throughput_rps": 12
    }
  ],
  "resource_estimate": { "gpu_memory_gb": 16, "kv_cache_gb_per_1024": 0.5 },
  "stability": { "deterministic": false, "sampling_stability_score": 0.87 },
  "compliance": { "redaction_supported": true, "pii_classification": "restricted" },
  "compatibility": { "backward_compatible_with": ["redwood/pythia-6k:2025-11-01"] },
  "published_at": "2026-01-15T18:32:00Z",
  "schema_checksum": "sha256:ab3f..."
}

Field guidance (high level):
- mcm_version: schema version. Increment for breaking schema changes.
- model_id: canonical model artifact identifier.
- capabilities: boolean + structured capability entries describing supported API features.
- performance_profiles: array; each entry includes name, sequence length bucket, and latency/throughput estimates measured under the standardized benchmark harness.
- resource_estimate: conservative runtime footprint estimates. Used by capacity planner and dedicated allocator.
- stability: numeric and boolean flags used by rollout policies (e.g., prefer deterministic variants for transactional workloads).
- compliance: tags for redaction, data classification, and any special licensing flags.
- compatibility: ledger of explicit compatibility guarantees for structured outputs.

2) Runtime discovery API
A lightweight HTTP endpoint is required on the model catalog service and on Local Private control plane sidecars: /v1/models/{model_id}/mcm (GET).
- GET returns the latest MCM JSON (cacheable up to TTL in response header).
- Runtime router may request the MCM during routing decisions; recommended cache TTL: 5 minutes for hosted, 1 minute for Dedicated control plane, configurable for Private.
- ETag and schema_checksum must be present for cheap validation.

3) Router contract and decision algorithm (summary)
When a request arrives, router computes candidate set filtered by: 1) must_support(requested_features) 2) tenant constraints (quota, region, policy) 3) capacity footprint.
Selection score = w_latency*expected_p50 + w_cost*estimated_token_cost + w_stability*(stability_score). Weights are runtime-configurable per-tenant.
Fallback ordering: prefer variants with compatible capability entries and higher stability score. If none compatible, route to safe-degraded variant and emit an observability event.

4) Onboarding and publication workflow
1) Author prepares model artifact and generates MCM using the onboarding CLI (redwood model publish --mcm mcm.json).
2) Preflight checks executed by onboarding service: schema validation, required performance_profiles for at least two seq_len buckets, resource_estimate sanity checks, and a smoke-generation test set.
3) If preflight passes, model is staged to canary pool and MCM published with state=staged.
4) After canary for N hours (default 24) and no regressions, operator promotes to state=published.

Operational requirements and SLOs
- MCM discovery endpoint SLO: 99.9% availability and 200ms p95 under production API load.
- Router lookup latency budget: MCM resolution must not add more than 2ms median to per-request routing decision (use local cache).
- Telemetry: every routing decision that uses an MCM must emit: model_id, mcm_version, profile_used, resolution_source (cache|catalog), and final_score.
- Alerting: if a majority (>50%) of routable variants for a model change resource_estimate by >20% within a 1h window, trigger capacity-warning paging to SRE.

Observability and Telemetry
- Required metrics and traces:
  - mcm.fetch.count, mcm.fetch.latency_ms (labels: model_id, source)
  - router.selection.count (labels: model_id, profile_name, tenant, resolution_source)
  - router.selection.latency_ms and router.score_components (for p50/p95 breakdown)
  - mcm.preflight.failures (by reason)
- Logging: structured event emitted for fallback due to capability_mismatch with fields: request_id, model_id, requested_features, candidate_models, chosen_model, reason.

Compatibility and Versioning
- MCM schema should remain backward compatible within a major version. Additive fields are allowed; renames/removals require a bump to mcm_version major.
- Runtimes must record mcm_version and schema_checksum in audit logs for every model decision.

Developer guidance and coding standards
- SDKs must provide first-class helpers: fetch_mcm(model_id) returns typed object; validate_mcm(mcm_json) throws on schema errors.
- Tests: any repository changing routing logic must include unit tests that mock MCM responses for at least three profiles: low-latency, high-throughput, long-context.
- Linting: onboarding CLI runs mcm-schema-lint during CI; failures block merge.

Infra standards and caching
- Cache topology: two-tier cache required:
  - Local in-memory per-router instance (TTL default 5m)
  - Shared catalog-backed LRU cache in control plane (TTL default 1m)
- Invalidation signals: On model publication or promotion, catalog must publish a model:mcm:updated pub/sub message including model_id and schema_checksum. Routers subscribe to infra bus to proactively invalidate local cache.

Performance and profiling playbook
- Benchmarking harness must produce the performance_profiles included in the MCM: defined runner, seed corpus, load shape, and measurement windows documented in /eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- Profiling guidance: when p95 deviates >30% from declared MCM p95 in production for 15m, create a perf-investigation ticket and tag as P1 if affecting more than 5% of requests.

Security and compliance notes
- Models marked with compliance.pii_classification = "restricted" require additional access checks in the router and must be excluded from cross-tenant routing.
- MCM manifests are signed by the onboarding service using a key managed in KMS; sidecars must validate signatures when trust_mode=strict.

Migration plan (for legacy models)
- Phase 1 (30 days): Require onboarding service to generate stub MCM for all existing published models with best-effort fields (capabilities: inferred).
- Phase 2 (60 days): Block new model promotion to published unless MCM includes at least: capabilities.generation, performance_profiles (one bucket), resource_estimate.
- Phase 3 (90 days): Enforce runtime routing that prefers models with valid MCM; emit warnings for requests routed to legacy models.

Governance and ownership
- Owner: Model Onboarding team (primary), Runtime Routing team (secondary).
- Review cadence: MCM schema and policy reviewed quarterly by Eng Standards board.

Appendix: Example CLI snippets
- Publish: redwood model publish --artifact s3://models/pythia-6k.tar.gz --mcm mcm.json
- Fetch locally: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://catalog.internal/v1/models/redwood/pythia-6k:2026-01-15/mcm

Appendix: Troubleshooting checklist (operational playbook)
1) If routers serve stale MCMs: check infra bus subscription, controller logs for model:mcm:updated, validate ETag behavior.
2) If preflight fails: run onboarding preflight locally with --verbose and attach failure trace to the model artifact ticket.
3) If routing scores differ across regions: verify catalog was fully promoted and checksummed; compare schema_checksum across control planes.
